# 5. Editor (ED)

The center area. This is the largest section, so it has 13 groups. Autocomplete is section 6.

13 groups, 568 features. Each feature lists its entry points and the pieces that finish it.

## ED-1 Editor groups, tabs and layout

(both). The tab strip and group grid with split, pin, preview, lock, new windows and editor switching. Examples: split editor and layout presets; pin, preview and keep-open tabs; move editor to a new window; Show All Editors.

50 features.

- Commands: workbench.action.showMultipleEditorTabs; workbench.action.showEditorTab; workbench.action.hideEditorTabs; workbench.action.editorActionsDefault; workbench.action.editorActionsTitleBar; workbench.action.hideEditorActions; workbench.action.showEditorActions; workbench.action.configureEditorTabs; workbench.action.configureEditor

- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\browser\actions\layoutActions.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\workbench.contribution.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editor.contribution.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorTitleControl.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\singleEditorTabsControl.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\noEditorTabsControl.ts; C bundle (all nine command ids and three settings found, showTabs default is multiple)
- Pieces:
  1. Right-clicking blank space in the tab strip opens a menu with a Tab Bar submenu that offers Multiple Tabs, Single Tab and Hidden with the current choice checked, and the same submenu sits under View > Appearance (`workbench.action.showMultipleEditorTabs`, `workbench.action.showEditorTab`, `workbench.action.hideEditorTabs`).
  2. Setting `workbench.editor.showTabs` chooses how editors show, with values `multiple` (one tab per editor, the default), `single` (the active editor as one large tab) and `none` (no title area).
  3. The Editor Actions Position submenu, in the tab strip menu and under View > Appearance, moves the editor action buttons to the Tab Bar, the Title Bar or Hidden with the current choice checked, and the Command Palette has Move Editor Actions to Title Bar, Move Editor Actions to Tab Bar, Hide Editor Actions and Show Editor Actions for the same choice (`workbench.action.editorActionsTitleBar`, `workbench.action.editorActionsDefault`, `workbench.action.hideEditorActions`, `workbench.action.showEditorActions`).
  4. Setting `workbench.editor.editorActionsLocation` chooses where editor actions show, with values `default` (the tab bar, or the title bar when tabs are hidden), `titleBar` and `hidden`.
  5. Setting `workbench.editor.alwaysShowEditorActions` chooses whether editor actions stay visible when the editor group is not active, off by default.
  6. Choosing Configure Tabs in the tab strip menu opens Settings filtered to the tab settings, and choosing Configure Editors in the editor title overflow menu opens Settings filtered to the editor settings (`workbench.action.configureEditorTabs`, `workbench.action.configureEditor`).

#### ED-1.7 Pin and unpin a tab

- Tag: both. Evidence: source. Boundary: no. Cursor: present
- What: The person pins a tab so it moves to the front of the strip, optionally shows it compact or on its own row, and keeps it from closing by keyboard or middle click.
- Commands: workbench.action.pinEditor; workbench.action.unpinEditor; workbench.action.toggleSeparatePinnedEditorTabs
- Menus: EditorTitleContext; CommandPalette
- Keys: Ctrl+K Shift+Enter (pins when the tab is not pinned, unpins when it is)
- Settings: workbench.editor.pinnedTabSizing; workbench.editor.pinnedTabsOnSeparateRow; workbench.editor.preventPinnedEditorClose
- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorCommands.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\actions\layoutActions.ts (Separate Pinned Editor Tabs); V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editor.contribution.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\workbench.contribution.ts; C bundle
- Pieces:
  1. Choosing Pin from the tab menu or the Command Palette pins the tab and moves it to the front of the strip, and the menu row then reads Unpin (`workbench.action.pinEditor`, `workbench.action.unpinEditor`).
  2. Pressing `Ctrl+K Shift+Enter` pins a tab that is not pinned and unpins one that is.

#### ED-1.8 Close one editor

- Tag: both. Evidence: source. Boundary: no. Cursor: present
- What: The person closes the active tab from its button, a middle click, the File menu or the keyboard, force-closes a pinned tab, or reverts and closes in one step.
- Commands: workbench.action.closeActiveEditor; workbench.action.closeActivePinnedEditor; workbench.action.revertAndCloseActiveEditor
- Menus: EditorTitleContext; EditorTitle; CommandPalette; MenubarFileMenu
- Keys: Ctrl+W (on Windows Ctrl+F4, with Ctrl+W as a second key); middle click on a tab
- Settings: workbench.editor.focusRecentEditorAfterClose; workbench.editor.closeOnFileDelete
- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorCommands.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorActions.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\multiEditorTabsControl.ts (middle click close); V\src\vs\workbench\browser\workbench.contribution.ts; C bundle
- Pieces:
  1. Clicking a tab's close button, or middle-clicking the tab, closes that editor.
  2. The Close row in the tab menu, File > Close Editor, the Command Palette and the keyboard close the active editor, using `Ctrl+F4` or `Ctrl+W` on Windows (`workbench.action.closeActiveEditor`).
  3. Close Active Pinned Editor closes a pinned tab even when the keyboard close is blocked for pinned tabs (`workbench.action.closeActivePinnedEditor`).
  4. Revert File and Close Editor discards unsaved changes and closes the active editor in one step (`workbench.action.revertAndCloseActiveEditor`).
  5. Setting `workbench.editor.focusRecentEditorAfterClose` chooses which tab becomes active after a close, the most recently used one when on (the default) or the next one from left to right when off.
  6. Setting `workbench.editor.closeOnFileDelete` chooses whether an editor closes by itself when its file is deleted or renamed by another process, off by default, and an editor with unsaved changes never closes this way.

#### ED-1.9 Close many editors or groups at once

- Tag: both. Evidence: source. Boundary: no. Cursor: present
- What: The person closes the other tabs, the tabs to the right or left, the saved tabs, every tab in the group, every tab in every group, or the whole group, and empty groups can close by themselves.

- Menus: EditorTitleContext; EditorTitle; CommandPalette; EmptyEditorGroup; EmptyEditorGroupContext
- Keys: Ctrl+K W (close all in group); Ctrl+K U (close saved); Ctrl+K Ctrl+W (close all editors); Ctrl+K Ctrl+Shift+W (close all groups); Ctrl+W on an empty group closes the group; Cmd+Alt+T on Mac for Close Others
- Settings: workbench.editor.closeEmptyGroups
- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorCommands.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editorActions.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\parts\editor\editor.contribution.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\browser\workbench.contribution.ts; C bundle (all eleven command ids found)
- Pieces:
  1. Choosing Close Others in the tab menu closes every other tab in the group, and the row is disabled when the group has one tab (`workbench.action.closeOtherEditors`, `Cmd+Alt+T` on Mac).
  2. Choosing Close to the Right in the tab menu closes the tabs after the clicked one and is disabled on the last tab or while several tabs are selected, and Close Editors to the Left in Group does the same on the other side from the Command Palette (`workbench.action.closeEditorsToTheRight`, `workbench.action.closeEditorsToTheLeft`).
  3. Choosing Close Saved, from the tab menu, the editor title overflow menu or `Ctrl+K U`, closes every tab in the group that has no unsaved changes (`workbench.action.closeUnmodifiedEditors`).
  4. Choosing Close All, from the tab menu, the editor title overflow menu or `Ctrl+K W`, closes every tab in the group (`workbench.action.closeEditorsInGroup`).
  5. Pressing `Ctrl+K Ctrl+W` closes every tab in every group (`workbench.action.closeAllEditors`).
  6. Pressing `Ctrl+K Ctrl+Shift+W` closes every tab and every group (`workbench.action.closeAllGroups`).
  7. Running `workbench.action.closeGroup` or `workbench.action.closeEditorsAndGroup` removes the active group, pressing `Ctrl+W` on an empty group closes it, and an empty group's menu and toolbar have a Close row.
  8. Close Editors in Other Groups and Close Editor in All Groups work from the Command Palette on the other groups, or on the same editor in every group (`workbench.action.closeEditorsInOtherGroups`, `workbench.action.closeEditorInAllGroups`).
  9. Setting `workbench.editor.closeEmptyGroups` chooses whether a group closes by itself when its last tab closes, on by default.

#### ED-3.18 Capture groups and escape codes in the replacement

- Tag: both. Evidence: source. Boundary: no. Cursor: present
- What: With regex on, the replacement can use $1 to $n and $& or $0 for matched text, $$ for a dollar, and the codes \n, \t, \\, \u, \U, \l and \L for new lines, tabs and upper or lower casing.
- Commands: none found
- Menus: none found
- Keys: none found
- Settings: none found
- Source: V\src\vs\editor\contrib\find\browser\replacePattern.ts (parseReplaceString, ReplacePattern.buildReplaceString); C bundle (method names buildReplaceString, hasReplacementPatterns; the individual escape codes were not read in the bundle)
- Pieces:
  1. With Use Regular Expression on, `$1` to `$99` in the replacement insert the text matched by that capture group, and `$&` or `$0` insert the whole match.
  2. `$$` in the replacement inserts a single dollar sign.
  3. `\n` in the replacement inserts a line break, `\t` inserts a tab, and `\\` inserts one backslash.
  4. `\u` or `\l` placed before a `$n` makes the first letter of the inserted text upper or lower case, and `\U` or `\L` makes all of it upper or lower case.
  5. With Use Regular Expression off, the replacement is inserted exactly as typed, and none of these codes apply.

  8. Setting `editor.minimap.autohide` chooses `none` (always shown, the default), `mouseover` (shown only while the pointer is over the minimap) or `scroll` (shown only while the editor is being scrolled).

#### ED-5.11 Fold or unfold the region at the cursor

- Tag: both. Evidence: source. Boundary: no. Cursor: present
- What: Collapse or expand the block the cursor is in, one level or all the way down, so you can hide code you are not reading.
- Commands: editor.fold; editor.unfold; editor.toggleFold; editor.foldRecursively; editor.unfoldRecursively; editor.toggleFoldRecursively
- Menus: CommandPalette
- Keys: Ctrl+Shift+[ (fold; Cmd+Alt+[ on macOS); Ctrl+Shift+] (unfold; Cmd+Alt+] on macOS); Ctrl+K Ctrl+L (toggle fold); Ctrl+K Ctrl+[ (fold recursively); Ctrl+K Ctrl+] (unfold recursively); Ctrl+K Ctrl+Shift+L (toggle fold recursively); all when the editor text has focus and folding is on

- Pieces:
  1. Fold (Ctrl+Shift+[, Cmd+Alt+[ on macOS) collapses the region the cursor is in, hiding its lines after the first.
  2. Unfold (Ctrl+Shift+], Cmd+Alt+] on macOS) expands the collapsed region at the cursor.
  3. Toggle Fold (Ctrl+K Ctrl+L) collapses the region at the cursor when it is open and expands it when it is collapsed.
  4. Fold Recursively (Ctrl+K Ctrl+[) collapses the region at the cursor and every region nested inside it.
  5. Unfold Recursively (Ctrl+K Ctrl+]) expands the region at the cursor and every region nested inside it.
  6. Toggle Fold Recursively (Ctrl+K Ctrl+Shift+L) flips the region at the cursor and everything nested inside it.
  7. All six commands are in the Command Palette, and the keys work only while the editor text has focus and folding is on (`editor.folding`).

  4. Setting `diffEditor.renderIndicators` chooses whether plus and minus marks show beside added and removed lines, with values true (default) and false.

  7. Setting `diffEditor.diffAlgorithm` chooses how differences are worked out, with values `legacy`, `advanced` (default), `advanced-external` and `advanced-wasm`.
  8. Settings `diffEditor.maxComputationTime` (milliseconds, default 5000, 0 for no timeout) and `diffEditor.maxFileSize` (megabytes, default 50, 0 for no limit) decide when the diff stops being computed for a slow or large file.
  9. Settings `diffEditor.experimental.useTrueInlineView` (default off) draws word changes inline in the inline view, and `diffEditor.experimental.showEmptyDecorations` (default on) shows marks where characters were inserted or deleted.

  7. Settings `workbench.colorTheme`, `workbench.preferredDarkColorTheme`, `workbench.preferredLightColorTheme`, `workbench.preferredHighContrastColorTheme` and `workbench.preferredHighContrastLightColorTheme` each hold a theme name, the active theme and the theme used for each system mode.
  8. Setting `window.autoDetectColorScheme` (default off) chooses whether the theme follows the system light or dark mode, and `window.autoDetectHighContrast` (default on) chooses whether it follows a high contrast operating system theme.
  9. Cursor adds its own built-in themes: Cursor Dark Midnight, Cursor Dark High Contrast, Cursor Dark, Cursor Light, Cursor Light Colorblind, Cursor Dark Colorblind and Cursor Light High Contrast. [cursor only]
  10. Try New Default Themes (`workbench.action.tryNewDefaultThemes`) is offered in the Command Palette. [stock only]

- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\contrib\workspace\browser\workspace.contribution.ts:745-790; V\src\vs\workbench\contrib\workspace\browser\workspaceTrustEditor.ts:669; V\src\vs\workbench\services\workspaces\common\workspaceTrust.ts; C bundle (module vs/workbench/contrib/workspace/browser/workspaceTrustEditor; `workbench.trust.manage` seen 7 times)
- Pieces:
  1. Manage Workspace Trust (`workbench.trust.manage`) opens a Workspace Trust editor tab whose header reads "You are in Restricted Mode" or, when trusted, "You trust this window", "You trust this folder" or "You trust this workspace".
  2. Trust and Don't Trust buttons in the header change the trust state of the window.
  3. A list under the header says what is on or off in Restricted Mode (tasks, debugging, workspace settings, extensions), with links to the affected settings and extensions.
  4. A Trusted Folders & Workspaces table with Host and Path columns lists the trusted places, with an Add Folder button and edit and delete icons on each row.
  5. Configure Workspace Trust Settings (`workbench.trust.configure`) opens the Settings editor filtered to the Workspace Trust settings.
  6. Setting `security.workspace.trust.enabled` turns Workspace Trust on or off, and in Cursor it is off by default, so Manage Workspace Trust and Configure Workspace Trust Settings are unavailable until it is on. [cursor only]
  7. Setting `security.workspace.trust.emptyWindow` chooses whether an empty window is trusted by default, on or off, default on.
  8. Setting `security.workspace.trust.startupPrompt` chooses when the startup trust prompt shows, with values `always`, `once` and `never` (the default).
  9. Setting `security.workspace.trust.banner` chooses when the Restricted Mode banner shows, with values `always`, `untilDismissed` (the default) and `never`.
  10. Setting `security.workspace.trust.untrustedFiles` chooses how untrusted files opened in a trusted workspace are handled, with values `prompt` (the default), `open` and `newWindow`.

- Source: V\src\vs\platform\request\common\request.ts (lines 236-361); V\src\vs\platform\request\node\requestService.ts (lines 85-143); V\src\vs\platform\windows\electron-main\windowImpl.ts (lines 1114-1132); V\src\vs\workbench\contrib\preferences\browser\settingsLayout.ts (lines 389-390); C bundle (the http configuration node with the six ids above, 0 hits for http.systemCertificatesNode)
- Pieces:
  1. The Settings editor table of contents has an Application > Proxy section that lists the `http.*` settings that apply to the app.
  2. Setting `http.proxy` takes a proxy URL starting with http, https, socks, socks4, socks4a, socks5 or socks5h (an empty value is allowed), and when it is empty the app uses the `http_proxy` and `https_proxy` environment variables.
  3. Setting `http.noProxy` lists domain names whose HTTP and HTTPS requests skip the proxy.
  4. Setting `http.proxyAuthorization` is sent as the `Proxy-Authorization` header on every request, and it is empty by default.
  5. Setting `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal` overrides the Kerberos service name used to sign in to the proxy, and when it is empty a name based on the proxy host is used.
  6. Setting `http.proxyStrictSSL` (on by default) checks the proxy server certificate against the trusted certificate authorities.
  7. Setting `http.systemCertificates` (on by default) loads trusted certificate authorities from the operating system, and on Windows and macOS turning it off needs a window reload.
  8. Setting `http.systemCertificatesNode` (experimental) loads the system certificates through Node.js built-in support and needs a window reload. [stock only]

  1. When a test fails with an error message, a small badge with the failed icon shows at the end of the failing line, and clicking it opens the peek view on that failure.
  2. A message that has a location is also drawn as faded text after the line, with line breaks turned into spaces and the text cut at 128 characters with an ellipsis, the line takes a color for the message severity, and hovering it shows the full message text.
  3. Clicking the faded message text opens the peek view when the message has output to show.
  4. The overview ruler gets a mark for the message, in the error color for errors and the info color for other messages.
  5. When the failure has expected and actual values, the badge reads "actual != expected" with each side shortened, and the expected and actual output views show small "Expected" and "Actual" labels above their lines.
  6. Editing the failing line or the code of its test removes the shown failure message until the test runs again.
  7. Running "Toggle Inline Test Output" (`testing.toggleInlineTestOutput`, `Ctrl+; Ctrl+I`) hides or shows the faded message text, it is listed in the Command Palette only when results exist, and the choice is remembered per workspace with the text shown by default.
  8. Setting `testing.showAllMessages` chooses whether messages from all test runs show or only the latest run, with values on and off, default off.
  9. Setting `testing.automaticallyOpenPeekView` chooses when the peek view opens by itself, with values `failureAnywhere`, `failureInVisibleDocument` and `never`, default `never`.
  10. Setting `testing.automaticallyOpenPeekViewDuringAutoRun` chooses whether the peek view also opens by itself during a continuous run, with values on and off, default off.

- Pieces:
  1. The peek view opens inside the editor titled "Test Output" and shows the failure message, the stack and, when there is one, a diff of expected and actual.
  2. It opens from "Peek Error" in the gutter menu, from clicking a failure badge or message text, or from the "Peek Test Output" link.
  3. Pressing `Alt+F8` or `Shift+Alt+F8` moves to the next or previous test failure in the file, listed as "Go to Next Test Failure" and "Go to Previous Test Failure" (`testing.goToNextMessage`, `testing.goToPreviousMessage`).
  4. A "Collapse Stack Frames" button folds the stack frames (`testing.collapsePeekStack`).
  5. An "Open in Editor" button opens the message in a full editor (`testing.openMessageInEditor`).
  6. "Toggle Test History in Peek" shows or hides the history of runs, on `Alt+H` while the peek is visible (`testing.toggleTestingPeekHistory`).
  7. Pressing `Escape` closes the peek view (`editor.closeTestPeek`), and a Close button closes it too.
  8. Setting `editor.stablePeek` chooses whether peek views stay open when you press `Escape`, with values on and off, default off.
  9. Buttons in the peek title come from the `TestPeekTitle` menu, and right-click entries on items in the peek come from the `TestPeekElement` menu.
  10. Running Peek Output (`testing.openOutputPeek`) from the Command Palette or pressing Ctrl+; then Ctrl+M opens an inline peek under the failing line in the editor, with the same run tree, message and output as the panel.

- Source: V\src\vs\workbench\contrib\testing\browser\codeCoverageDecorations.ts; V\src\vs\workbench\contrib\testing\common\configuration.ts; C bundle (module testing/browser/codeCoverageDecorations)
- Pieces:
  1. After a run with coverage, covered lines in the file are tinted green and uncovered lines red, in the text and in the gutter.
  2. Hovering a tinted line, function or branch says how often it ran, for example "`{name}` was executed {n} time(s)." or "Branch {n} in {text} was not covered."
  3. A sticky bar at the top center of the editor shows the file's coverage bars with a Show Inline or Hide Inline button and a Rerun button that is disabled while the run is going.
  4. Pressing `Ctrl+; Ctrl+Shift+I` runs "Toggle Inline Coverage" (`testing.toggleInlineCoverage`) and turns the tinting on or off, and when the bar is off an editor title button does the same.
  5. The bar shows "{n} test(s) ran code in this file" with a button that filters the coverage to one test, and when the bar is off the same filter is an editor title button (`testing.coverageFilterToTestInEditor`).
  6. "Show Test Coverage Toolbar" (`testing.coverageToggleToolbar`), listed in the Command Palette and the editor title while coverage is open, shows or hides the bar by flipping `testing.coverageToolbarEnabled`, with values on and off, default off.
  7. Setting `testing.displayedCoveragePercent` chooses which percentage the coverage bars show, with values `totalCoverage`, `statement` and `minimum`, default `totalCoverage`.
  8. Setting `testing.coverageBarThresholds` sets the percentages where the coverage bars turn red, yellow and green, default 0, 60 and 90.
  9. Pressing `Alt+F9` or `Shift+Alt+F9`, or using the arrow buttons on the bar, jumps to the next or previous uncovered line, listed as "Go to Next Uncovered Line" and "Go to Previous Uncovered Line" (`testing.coverage.goToNextMissedLine`, `testing.coverage.goToPreviousMissedLine`). [stock only]
  10. Setting `testing.coverageMinimapEnabled` chooses whether coverage marks show on the minimap, with values on and off, default on. [stock only]
